sections.title: Reading Comprehension · Passage B
sections.intro: Read “Big Jigsaw” and answer questions 11–14. A vocabulary note follows the poem.

passage.title: Big Jigsaw
passage.credit: —Chris Forhan · “Big Jigsaw” · from The New American Poets: A Bread Loaf Anthology (2000), University Press of New England

lines.text: I’ve hunched so long above this puzzle
laid out on my gouged and ink-stained workbench,
I think, at last, it’s unsolvable,
that the only meaning it holds is told
in the moments I feel on the verge
of understanding, and it turns me back.
The pieces: so small, so many. How they
belong together is beyond me,
though early on my mind inclined
toward an idyllic scene: a yellow field,
all jonquils,¹ a sea, the wide horizon…
The dog’s dish is empty. My wife and children
sleep. The house is hushed, except
for the stout hall clock that ticks its minutes.
Here in my patch of lamplight, time
dawdles, waiting for me to catch up,
though a few small hairs on my wrist
have gone white, and evening’s blank encircles me.
Who made this puzzle? If I sought him out
would he hear my plea and reveal its logic?
But the hour is late, my vision strained.
How could I look for him now, though he were
waiting for me, and knew me by name?
¹ jonquils — a type of yellow daffodil

questions.prompt: The opening stanza conveys a sense of
questions.explanation: After long work, the speaker thinks the puzzle may be unsolvable and says each near-understanding turns him back. That repeated failure conveys frustration.

questions.prompt: As used in the poem, the word “idyllic” (line 10) most nearly means
questions.explanation: The imagined scene has a yellow field, flowers, a sea, and a wide horizon. These pleasing images make “idyllic” mean charmingly beautiful.

questions.prompt: In lines 15 and 16, the phrase “time/dawdles, waiting for me to catch up” implies that the narrator is

choices.text: wishing the family would wake up
annoyed by the stillness of the night

questions.explanation: Absorbed in the puzzle, the speaker feels as if time itself slows and waits for his mind. This suggests deep preoccupation with his thoughts.

questions.prompt: In the context of the poem as a whole, the jigsaw puzzle represents
questions.explanation: The speaker searches for the puzzle’s meaning, notices aging and the passing of time, and wonders whether its maker knows him. The puzzle becomes a metaphor for trying to understand human existence.
